article_title: Integrating Attentional Factors and Spacing in Logistic Knowledge Tracing Models to Explore the Impact of Training Sequences on Category Learning
citation: Meng Cao, Wei Chu, Philip I. Pavlik Jr., Liang Zhang. (2024). Integrating Attentional Factors and Spacing in Logistic Knowledge Tracing Models to Explore the Impact of Training Sequences on Category Learning. https://osf.io/t8wzy/
title: A two-factor computational account: LKT models integrating attentional comparison counts with ACT-R-based spacing features to explain interleaving/blocking effects
description: This framework extends the logistic knowledge tracing (LKT) modeling framework by simultaneously adding attentional features and spacing features. Attention is operationalized by counting adjacent-trial comparisons: "we recorded the counts of comparisons with each preceding trial, considering whether it be- longs to the same or different category". Spacing is captured with ppe, base4, and recency features rooted in the ACT-R memory model's power-law decay of forgetting. Cross-validated on two datasets, the integrated attention-based AFM with ppe best predicted posttest performance, "bridging the gap between attentional factors and memory processes" in line with Yan and colleagues' two-stage framework.
requirements: Requires sequence-level log data recording trial order so same- vs. different-category comparisons and inter-trial timing can be computed for each knowledge component.
constraints: The current model primarily focuses on the training sequence and spacing without incorporating the similarity parameters; the article states adding the similarity feature "falls beyond the scope of the current paper".
The current datasets only feature short retention intervals, with the posttest immediately following the learning session.
target_learners: Adult learners in inductive category learning tasks (Amazon Mechanical Turk workers and undergraduate students)
target_learning_goals: Category learning and generalization to novel exemplars
Accurate prediction of student performance under interleaved vs. blocked training sequences
examples: The bird dataset used five block-size levels from 1 (fully interleaving) to 16 (fully blocking), with 160 learning trials and a 60-item posttest including 20 novel stimuli.
